questions.explain: Constrained vCPUs let a VM deploy with fewer active vCPUs than the hardware provides — e.g., 16 core licenses on a 64-vCPU VM — while keeping the larger size's memory and disk throughput, combined with Azure Hybrid Benefit for compute-only billing.
options: Pay-as-you-go vCore billing with no license options
Constrained vCPUs, letting you size the license footprint independently of memory and throughput
Free Developer Edition on all VM sizes
License Mobility through AWS
questions.q: What is the unique licensing lever for SQL Server on Azure VMs described in the chapter?

questions.explain: The chapter's rules: data files get ReadOnly caching (local SSD accelerates reads), log volumes get no caching (None) because write-through latency matters — the most commonly misconfigured setting.
options: Data: ReadWrite, Log: ReadOnly
Data: ReadOnly, Log: None
Data: None, Log: ReadOnly
Data: ReadWrite, Log: ReadWrite
questions.q: What are the correct Azure storage caching policies for SQL Server data and log volumes?

questions.explain: The load balancer holds the listener IP as a frontend with a health probe (conventionally TCP 59999) answered only by the primary, plus floating IP (direct server return). The chapter calls this the architectural piece with no EC2 equivalent and the most common source of 'AG works, listener doesn't' incidents.
options: To encrypt traffic between replicas
Because without the load balancer, cross-subnet listener failover does not work on Azure
To replace the Windows cluster
To provide backup storage for the AG
questions.q: Why does the AG listener on Azure VMs sit behind an internal Azure Load Balancer?

questions.explain: Azure VMs have an ephemeral temp drive (D:) backed by local SSD — fast and free. Pointing tempdb at D: gives maximum tempdb throughput at zero storage cost; it's safe because tempdb is recreated on SQL Server start anyway.
options: On the OS disk C:
On a Premium SSD data volume
On the ephemeral temp drive D:, backed by free local SSD
In Azure Blob storage
questions.q: Where should tempdb be placed on an Azure VM, per the chapter?

questions.explain: The cloud witness is a blob storage endpoint that holds the quorum vote, replacing the file-share witness — no third VM or SMB share to manage; it's the deciding vote for two-replica AGs.
options: A third VM running as witness
An Azure cloud witness — a blob storage endpoint holding the quorum vote
A quorum disk on shared storage
The Azure Load Balancer health probe
questions.q: What replaces the file-share witness for quorum in an Always On AG on Azure VMs?
